name: Courtyard by Marriott
summary: Arches, columns, cornices, a balustrade and jali screens for a hotel facade.
description: A classical front for the Courtyard by Marriott hotel in Bengaluru. Tall arched openings run along the ground floor between full-height columns, and the entrance porch is topped with a moulded cornice and a balustrade.
Beside the hotel sign, a row of geometric jali screens stands in front of the glazing, adding pattern while letting light through to the floors behind.

Balustrade along the top of the porch

name: 1 MG-Lido Mall
summary: Fluted Corinthian columns and carved ornamental panels for a mall facade.
description: A classical treatment for the facade of 1 MG-Lido Mall. Fluted columns with Corinthian capitals rise past two floors of glazing, set against the building's beige walls.
Between the columns, carved panels with a shell-and-scroll motif sit above and below the windows, and a white cornice runs along the top of the ground floor.

description: A full-width jali screen with a star pattern covers the upper front of the Royal Convention Centre in Mysuru. In the evening the hall's lights shine through it, so the pattern glows from inside.
White pilaster panels frame the entrance and carry the centre's name.

name: Aero One
summary: Full-height jali screens running up a residential tower.
description: Bands of white jali screens run the full height of Aero One, a residential tower in Devanahalli. Two continuous bands on each face climb from the podium to the roof between the rows of windows.
The geometric pattern breaks up the height of the tower and stands out against its darker walls.
